name: ESP32-P4-NANO

usb.notes: The Type-C port goes through a CH343P to UART0 (GPIO37/38). The Type-A port is USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG on dedicated pads, not GPIOs.

verification.notes: I2C, Ethernet, SD and audio pins from the wiki's ESP-IDF sections. Wi-Fi coprocessor SDIO pins from the demo's 08_eth2ap sdkconfig. CH343P on GPIO37/38 from the schematic. The old /wiki/ESP32-P4-Nano URL returns 404. BOOT on GPIO35 comes from the datasheet (GPIO35 is the download-mode strap). Chip revision v1 from the wiki FAQ (ECO1 chip).

peripherals.notes: dout = P4 to codec DSDIN, din = codec ASDOUT to P4.
Power amplifier enable, active high. Speaker on an MX1.25 2P connector.
The demo powers the card IO from an on-chip LDO channel (sd_pwr_ctrl). Which channel, and whether a GPIO switches card power, is not documented.
Internal EMAC over RMII, PHY address 1 (demo Kconfig). REF_CLK is a 50 MHz clock from the PHY. Optional PoE module.
Wi-Fi 6 / Bluetooth 5 coprocessor. Use esp_wifi_remote + esp_hosted (SDIO host). rst drives the C6 enable.

warnings: Chip revision matters: the wiki FAQ says this board ships with an ECO1 (v1.x) chip, so the profile builds for revision < 3.0. Check with `wsesp.py detect`. If esptool reports v3.x, set chip_revision to v3. Firmware for one does not boot on the other.
GPIO35 is both the BOOT button and Ethernet RMII TXD1. Don't hold BOOT while Ethernet is running, and don't attach anything that pulls GPIO35 low at reset.
GPIO34 (RMII TXD0) and GPIO35 are strapping pins used by Ethernet. GPIO36-38 are also strapping pins (37/38 are UART0).

The wiki lists the RMII data lines as 'TXD[1:0]: GPIO34 and GPIO35' and 'RXD[1:0]: GPIO30 and GPIO29', which reads as TXD1=34. The ESP32-P4 IO MUX table has GPIO34=TXD0 and GPIO35=TXD1. The profile follows the datasheet.
Wiki FAQ: on the ECO1 chip the ADC is not calibrated (readings are unreliable) and USB Serial/JTAG (GPIO24/25) is not supported.

The schematic shows a GPIO45 net near the microSD section, and the newer ESP32-P4-NANO-WIFI6-DB uses GPIO45 as SD power enable, but the NANO docs don't say what GPIO45 does here. Leave it alone until confirmed.
The header pinout is only published as an image on the wiki, so free_pins is not filled in.
